name: Internship Platform — iOS 26 × Zemingo
context: Internal operational product for Zemingo's design internship program. Built July 2026.
summary: An internal multi-user platform for running Zemingo's design internship program, taken from product definition and a functional Tailwind prototype through an iOS 26-inspired visual redesign and a final Zemingo-branded interface.
challenge: Three interns, their mentors and a team leader needed one shared system for program milestones, task progress, hour logging and mentor feedback — with role-based access and real privacy rules around mentor-authored evaluation content.
objectives: Give interns, mentors and team leaders a single operational system.
Enforce feedback privacy at the database layer rather than in the UI.
Ship functional behaviour before visual polish, then redesign deliberately.
responsibilities: Owned product concept, requirements and scope.
Defined roles, permissions, feedback privacy and core information architecture.
Designed the internship program structure and mentor feedback framework.
Directed AI-assisted implementation through repo-grounded specifications and autonomous coding workflows.
Iterated the product across multiple versions based on product and UX decisions.
Led the visual transformation from a functional Tailwind UI to an iOS 26-inspired design language and then to a Zemingo-branded system.

process.title: Product definition
process.description: Defined the internship workflow, the three-tier role model, milestones, task tracking, hours logging and mentor feedback requirements.

process.title: Architecture and functional build
process.description: Specified a Next.js / TypeScript / Supabase architecture with PostgreSQL row-level security, Google Workspace authentication and Vercel deployment. Functional behaviour was prioritised over visual polish — the first interface was deliberately plain.

process.title: AI-native implementation loop
process.description: Turned product decisions into repo-anchored build instructions with exact implementation details, migrations and acceptance criteria, then directed autonomous agents to execute them. The distinctive part is the loop — decide, specify, execute, critique, iterate — not the code generation itself.

process.title: UX iteration
process.description: Simplified the product across successive versions: reorganised the intern experience into Tasks and Feedback, evolved the rating model, removed unnecessary functionality, and preserved existing data through migrations rather than resetting.

process.title: iOS 26 design-language pass
process.description: Transformed the plain functional prototype using an iOS 26-inspired system: grouped surfaces, pill geometry, segmented controls, soft glass-like shadows, system typography and iOS-derived design tokens.

process.title: Zemingo brand layer
process.description: Applied a brand layer over the iOS-inspired structure: Zemingo typography, brand accents, selection states, progress styling and wordmark treatment.

process.title: Making-of narrative
process.description: Built a dedicated visual narrative presenting the transformation explicitly as Code → First Interface → iOS 26 → Zemingo → Final Product.

outcomes: A working multi-user internship-management platform, supporting intern, mentor and team-leader workflows.
Feedback privacy enforced at the database layer through PostgreSQL row-level security rather than in the interface.
A bilingual feedback and evaluation framework, including RTL support.
A functional product transformed into a deliberately branded visual system — not a static portfolio mockup.

conversation_hooks.recruiter_intent: How does Boaz actually use AI in his work?
conversation_hooks.agent_response_goal: This is the strongest end-to-end evidence: product decisions → implementation-ready spec → autonomous execution → critique → iteration → design-system transformation. Lead with the loop, not the tooling.

conversation_hooks.recruiter_intent: Can Boaz work beyond traditional product design?
conversation_hooks.agent_response_goal: Show the span — product definition, UX, architecture, data and privacy decisions, implementation direction, visual design — without overstating independent coding depth. He directed the implementation; he is not being presented as a full-stack engineer.

conversation_hooks.recruiter_intent: Show me a product-design case study.
conversation_hooks.agent_response_goal: Open with the operational problem and the role model, then the UX decisions, then the interface evolution. The technical stack comes last — it is context, not the point.
Show the Code → Tailwind → iOS 26 → Zemingo transformation. This is the clearest visual-craft evidence in the portfolio because the same product is visible at every stage.

presentation.short_pitch: An AI-native internal product taken from requirements and architecture to a working multi-user platform, then redesigned from a functional Tailwind prototype into an iOS 26-inspired, Zemingo-branded experience.
presentation.long_pitch: The interesting part is not that a dashboard was restyled. It is the sequence: an operational problem became a product definition, then a functional system built through an AI-native delivery loop, then a deliberate visual transformation through two design languages. Boaz owned the product decisions and directed the implementation rather than writing it himself.
